title: Precheck framework in redwood-private-installer (pluggable checks, severities, JSON report)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Problem
Private upgrades are failing late (during chart apply / migrations) due to missing prerequisites (k8s version, disk, permissions, storage class, etc.). We need a consistent precheck framework that:
- is pluggable (easy to add checks over time)
- supports severity levels (blocker vs warn vs info)
- emits a machine-readable JSON report for Support/PS ingestion and diagnostics bundles
- has a sane CLI UX for operators (human readable summary + remediation hints)

Scope
Implement a precheck runner framework inside `redwood-private-installer`.

Key requirements
1) Check interface + registry
- Provide a small interface that checks implement (name/id, description, severity, run(ctx) -> result).
- Checks should be registered in a central registry (explicit list) to keep ordering deterministic.
- Runner must support grouping (e.g., cluster, storage, permissions) for output/readability.

2) Severity model
- Define severity enum: BLOCKER | WARN | INFO.
- Runner should exit non-zero if any BLOCKER check fails.
- WARN failures should not block upgrade, but should be surfaced prominently.
- INFO is purely informational.

3) Standardized result shape
Each check result must include:
- id (stable string, e.g., `k8s.version`, `disk.free-space`)
- title (short)
- severity (BLOCKER/WARN/INFO)
- status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP)
- message (short human readable)
- remediation (actionable hint; optional but strongly encouraged)
- evidence (freeform string array; e.g., detected version, detected storage class)
- duration_ms

4) JSON report output
- `--json` flag outputs full report to stdout.
- `--output-file <path>` writes JSON to disk (used by diagnostics bundle and Support workflows).
- JSON output must be stable across versions; changes should be additive.

5) CLI integration + operator UX
- Add a top-level command `precheck` (or `upgrade precheck`) that can be run independently of upgrade.
- Human output should include: summary counts (pass/fail), blockers first, remediation hints, and a final recommended action.
- Support `--skip <check_id>` for break-glass scenarios (must annotate report as skipped + include in summary).
- Support `--strict` (treat WARN as BLOCKER) for SRE staging rehearsals.

6) Initial checks (MVP)
Implement a small initial set to validate framework end-to-end:
- Kubernetes version compatibility (BLOCKER)
- Disk free space on installer host / target nodes (BLOCKER or WARN depending on threshold)
- RBAC/permissions to list/get pods + create jobs in target namespace (BLOCKER)

Non-goals
- Building all prechecks in this ticket (additional checks will follow in ENG-2314 sub-work).
- Auto-remediation.

Implementation notes
- Keep output schema versioned via `report_schema_version` field (e.g., `1`).
- Ensure the runner collects timings and continues running WARN/INFO checks even if a blocker fails (so operator sees full picture). Exception: allow `--fail-fast` for CI-only usage.
- Checks must run with a common context that includes: kubeconfig path, target namespace, release name, and current/target version (when available).

Acceptance criteria
- A pluggable framework exists in `redwood-private-installer` and is used by the `precheck` command.
- At least 3 initial checks are implemented and covered by unit tests (mocked k8s client where appropriate).
- Human-readable output includes clear remediation hints.
- JSON report output includes all required fields and is written with `--output-file`.
- Exit code behavior matches severity rules (BLOCKER => non-zero; WARN => zero unless `--strict`).

References
- Initiative: ENG-2314 (upgrade workflow)
- Compatibility enforcement: ENG-2315
- Related PRs (expected): redwood-private-installer PR for precheck runner (see GitHub tracking once opened)
comments: 2025-01-16 (Devon Price): Drafted interfaces: `Check`, `Result`, `Runner`. Proposing explicit registry list to keep ordering deterministic for operator output + Support comparisons.

2025-01-17 (Ethan Park): +1 on deterministic ordering. Please ensure the runner can collect `current_versions` from control plane when available, but does not require it (so it works pre-install / broken control plane scenarios).

2025-01-21 (Sean Gallagher): SRE ask: add `--strict` (warns become blockers) and include duration per check so we can alert on precheck regressions. Also prefer runner does NOT stop at first failure; we need the full list for incident triage.
2025-01-24 (Kenji Nakamura): UX note: human output should group by category and show "Next action" at the end (e.g., "Fix BLOCKER checks then re-run"). Avoid dumping raw JSON unless requested.
2025-01-29 (Devon Price): Implemented MVP checks: k8s version, disk free space, RBAC can-i. Added `--json` and `--output-file`. Follow-up: align check IDs with docs naming conventions.

2025-02-03 (Connor O'Brien): Please ensure `--skip` is clearly annotated in both human and JSON output; break-glass needs to be obvious in Support artifacts. Also add `report_schema_version` for future-proofing.

2025-02-07 (Devon Price): Opened PR: redwood-private-installer/pr_421 (precheck runner framework + initial checks). Added schema version, durations, summary counts, exit codes. Requesting review from Sean + Ethan.

2025-02-10 (Jacob Stein): Supportability: JSON output looks good. Request adding `invocation_id` (uuid) so precheck report can be linked to diagnostics bundle + upgrade correlation id later (ENG-2321). Devon agreed to add.
2025-02-12 (Devon Price): Merged PR. Added `invocation_id` and improved remediation messages. Closing ticket; additional checks to be tracked under ENG-2314/ENG-2321.
